links.outcome: Staff reliance, perceived clinical loss and operational relief after AI tool withdrawal
links.effect: Of 40 respondents, 35% perceived logistical burden post-decommissioning; among 5 reporting staff, two voiced disappointment at withdrawal and one had grown reliant on the tool; free text showed both loss of clinical value and operational relief.
links.quote: Response rate from reporting staff was low (5 of 40), with two voicing disappointment in AI tool withdrawal, and one stating they had grown reliant on the tool.

links.outcome: Staff-perceived disruption and benefit after decommissioning of chest radiograph AI triage tool
links.effect: Perceived patient benefit stable (70% vs 71.1% pre-implementation); logistical burden 35% (14 of 40) post-decommissioning, versus 26.4% late implementation and 51.7% early implementation.
links.quote: Decommissioning produces both operational relief and perceived clinical loss, with effects differing by staff role.

unlisted_practices: Post-decommissioning staff survey on emotional burden and future AI engagement

screen.reason: Empirical survey of clinical staff following the real-world decommissioning/off-boarding of a chest radiograph AI triage tool, examining the operational and workflow impact of tool withdrawal.

primary.practice: AI tool decommissioning and off-boarding management
